title: The new ordinariness of Rahul Gandhi
subtitle: A sample subtitle for the fixture

body_html:
The protest began on a Monday and did not stop for three days. Its leader walked at the front, in a white T-shirt, and the cameras walked with him.1 Nobody could say what it was for, and that was the point the crowd seemed to enjoy.

Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts.

A dance in the head

“There is a difference,” a party worker told me, “between being ordinary and being seen to be ordinary.” He meant it kindly. The second kind of ordinariness has to be staged, and staging is a craft with its own rules and its own costs.

That craft is what the next year will test, far more than any single speech or march through the old city in the heat.

1

The march route was announced the night before.
